age_range.raw_age_text: 15 yrs +

description: Join us for a community talk for Breast Cancer Awareness Month. Breast Surgeon Dr. Irene Israel from Advocate Medical Group will discuss topics that include: breast health, risk factors for breast cancer, the basics of breast cancer and how it impacts you. This wellness series talk is free for fitness members, please register at the Main Service Desk at Fort Hill. (km)

name: Wellness Series: Heart Health

age_range.raw_age_text: 15 yrs +

description: Join us for a community talk on Heart Disease and Heart Health. Dr. Jeffrey Ziffra of Advocate Good Samaritan Hospital will discuss blood pressure goals for cardiovascular disease protection, the benefits of cardiovascular exercise, diet and cholesterol recommendations and how to detect cardiac disease. This wellness series talk is free for fitness members, please register at the Main Service Desk at Fort Hill. (km)

name: Winter Break: 5 Star Soccer Camp

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 5 yrs but less than 11 yrs

description: The 5 Star Soccer Camps offer a fresh, enthusiastic approach to teaching youth soccer. Our curriculum presents the most current and advanced information on the development of the youth soccer player. Our quality staff builds on fundamental techniques while creating an atmosphere that unlocks the game within each child. We believe in our program, designed for success, that presents a positive, enjoyable environment for learning from proven coaches in youth soccer.(sa)

name: Winter Break: Chess Wizards

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 5 yrs but less than 13 yrs

description: Chess Wizards is a premier chess education company providing fun, informative and challenging chess experiences. They provide an interactive, discovery-based curriculum to inspire students to think ahead, visualize their goals, win graciously and accept defeat with dignity and sportsmanship. This multi-day winter break camp is geared to suit children of all skill levels with a goal of helping participants build their knowledge and chess-playing confidence through lessons and tournament play while having fun! (bd)

name: Winter Break: Dinosaur Adventures Mini Camp

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 5 yrs but less than 9 yrs

description: There's an explorer in all of us and if you're ready for an expedition in dinosaur discovery, this is for you! T-Rexplorers take you on an adventure straight from the Cretaceous period with this unique, hands-on exploration of dinosaur science and paleontology. Hold real dinosaur bones like those seen in museums! Conduct investigations of different authentic dinosaur fossil types from species like Triceratops and T-Rex. Enjoy discovery, humor, fun, games and an activity or craft to take home. You'll be going outdoors (weather permitting) so dress accordingly. Please bring lunch, snack and water bottle. (bd)

name: Winter Break: Gymnastics Camps

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 15 yrs

description: Learn and develop new gymnastics/tumbling skills. Enjoy a variety of games and meet new friends. All experience levels are welcome; campers are grouped by skill level. Please bring water each day. (dn)

name: Winter Break: Kids First Badminton Camp

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 7 yrs but less than 15 yrs

description: Experienced coaches from Kids First Sports Safety, Inc. teach badminton fundamentals using competitive drills that develop skills. Grip, racquet positioning, serving, body balance and first-step directional movement are emphasized. Camp concludes with a skills challenge and championship game. All equipment is provided. (ba)

name: Winter Break: Kids First Baseball/Softball Skills Camp

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 13 yrs

description: Brush up on the fundamentals of baseball/softball and have fun improving batting, throwing, fielding and base running skills and learning all about teamwork. Camp concludes with a championship game. Taught by Kids First Sports Safety, Inc. Players should bring their own glove and wear gym shoes; cleats are not allowed in the gym. (ba)

name: Winter Break: Kids First Basketball Camp

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 5 yrs but less than 13 yrs

description: Basketball games plus fundamentals make this holiday camp special! Experienced coaches from Kids First Sports Safety, Inc. teach basketball skills and safety to get you game ready. Camp offers skills contests and championship games. Skills to include: shooting, dribbling, passing, speed and quickness, body balance, first step directional movements and floor spacing. Basketball safety awareness and sportsmanship also will be covered. (ba)

name: Winter Break: Kids First Cheerleading Skills Camp

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 5 yrs but less than 15 yrs

description: Experienced coaches teach cheerleading skills using fun drills to enhance techniques. Body balance, timing, rhythm, pom-pom bebop dance, jumps, stunts, cheers, rah-rah awareness and sportsmanship are emphasized. Camp concludes with a performance for parents on the final day. Conducted by Kids First Sports Safety, Inc. (ba)

name: Winter Break: Kids First Dodgeball Camp

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 7 yrs but less than 14 yrs

description: Have a blast running, throwing, dodging and ducking your way to victory! Camp features many types of games and matches each day with a championship match on the last day. Only safe, gator-skin balls are used. Taught by Kids First Sports Safety, Inc. (ba)

name: Winter Break: Kids First Flag Football Camp

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 14 yrs

description: Touchdown! Spend your break learning and practicing fundamental football skills and strategies. Indoor flag football equipment is used to teach the techniques of the sport through drills and scrimmages. A championship game is played on the last day. This camp is conducted by Kids First Sports Safety, Inc. (ba)

name: Winter Break: Kids First Multi-Sport Camp

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 14 yrs

description: Experienced coaches teach different sports each day giving kids a chance to learn about new sports and play their favorites. General rules are introduced including safety and fundamentals, and then the game is played. Choices may include basketball, baseball/softball, soccer, flag football, T-ball/Blast ball, kickball, dodgeball and balloon ball. (ba)

name: Winter Break: Kids First Speed Training Camp

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 15 yrs

description: Coaches focus on teaching sprints, hurdles, jumps, running and throws in a safe and fundamental way. The program consists of body-balance techniques and speed, quickness and agility drills designed to produce a safer, more powerful athlete. A series of team relay races makes the program fun and entertaining. Conducted by Kids First Sports Safety, Inc. (ba)

name: Winter Break: Kids First Track and Field Camp

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 5 yrs but less than 15 yrs

description: Camp introduces many of the events that make up the sport of track and field. Learn new techniques and strengthen existing skills. Focus is on teaching the basics of sprints, hurdles, jumps, quickness and throws in a safe and fundamental way. There is a mini-meet at the end of the week. Conducted by Kids First Sports Safety, Inc. (ba)

name: Winter Break: Kids First Ultimate Frisbee® Camp

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 7 yrs but less than 15 yrs

description: Kids First Sports Safety, Inc. certified coaches prepare players to play, enjoy and win in a team concept at Ultimate Frisbee® - one of the fastest growing team sports in the country! Ultimate can be described as a combination of soccer, football and basketball. It's a simple-to-learn, yet demanding game. Offensive and defensive drills are supplemented by games leading to a championship match on the final day. (ba)

name: Winter Break: Kids First Volleyball Basics Camp

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 14 yrs

description: Players learn fundamental volleyball techniques incorporating balance, directional movement, ball handling and sportsmanship. Excellent coaches prepare kids to succeed using drills, games and instruction each day. Conducted by Kids First Sports Safety, Inc. staff. (ba)

name: Winter Break: RoboThink STEM Robotics Camp

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 7 yrs but less than 13 yrs

description: This winter break, build amazing robots and engage in robotic challenges and games! Equipped with RoboThink's innovative kits, including gears, motors, sensors and mainboards, campers build and play with robots of all shapes, sizes and functions. Instructors take participants on a fun journey, learning about robotics principles and problem solving. The activities are interactive, hands-on and engaging to promote learning in a fun way. Different content will be taught at each camp, so participants can register for either or both sessions. (bd)

name: Winter Break: Sewing Camp

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 8 yrs but less than 18 yrs

description: Join us for an introductory sewing class! Participants will learn how to thread a machine, wind a bobbin, and sew straight lines. Sewing machines will be provided for use in class. If you have your own working sewing machine, you are welcome to bring it. All supplies needed will be provided by the instructor. Supply fee is $20 payable to instructor at first class. (bd)

name: Winter Break: The STEAM Team

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 5 yrs but less than 13 yrs

description: Get ready to have some scientific fun and join our Winter Break STEAM Team! This three-day adventure will have your future scientists exploring different Chemical, Physical, and Life Sciences. On our final day they get to have a parent or guardian join them for the final hour as they get to recreate and teach you how to do their favorite experiment they learned while with us all week! Lab coats and goggles are included. Please bring a nut-free snack and spill proof water bottle. We will have a snack break each day. (bd)

name: Winter Break: Volleyball EVP Camps

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 8 yrs but less than 15 yrs

description: Join us for a special holiday volleyball camp session taught and directed by EVP Academy Pros. The 3-day camp will concentrate on the fundamentals of passing, setting, spiking and overhand serve. The lesson plan directs the use of self-mastery training that helps each student reach a new level. The knowledge of the instructors will give the participants a head start on their skills in preparation for club team play. (ba)

name: Winter Break: Young Rembrandts Double the Fun Drawing

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 5 yrs but less than 13 yrs

description: Here's an exciting experience for your imaginative child that is sure to awaken their inner artist! We'll explore all the basics of visual arts in a fun and confident setting that ensures success for every child, focusing on basic drawing, portraits, action, and cartooning. Students complete several different projects and learn to draw whimsical characters, animals, everyday objects, and action scenes. Young Rembrandts artists gain so much confidence. Double your child's creative spirit and art skills. Add this camp to your child's schedule. Don't miss out, sign up today! (bd)

age_range.raw_age_text: 16 yrs +

description: Our PGA professionals offer instructional clinics catering to both beginning and intermediate women golfers that include instruction on full swing, pitching, chipping, putting, rules and etiquette. Receive a lesson guide and a four-token range punch card - a $60 value. The first and second lessons are scheduled for two hours; the third and fourth lessons are scheduled for one hour. Participants should provide their own clubs. A fairway wood, the 5, 7, 9 irons and a putter are recommended. We have a limited number of regulation golf clubs available at no charge that can be reserved on a first come, first served basis by contacting the Golf Shop where the lesson is held. You also are eligible for a discount on club purchases in our Golf Shops. For rainout information, call the Naperbrook Golf Shop at 630-378-4215. (ml, dh)

description: Yoga Gold is a yoga class choreographed specifically for the Active Older Adult (AOA). This class will move your whole body through a complete series of seated and standing yoga poses. Chair support is offered to safely perform a variety of postures designed to increase flexibility, balance and range of motion. (km)

name: Yoga: Beginner/Intermediate

age_range.raw_age_text: 16 yrs +

description: Yoga for Beginners/Intermediate level students is the perfect class for individuals just starting a yoga practice or for those with some basic experience and knowledge. This small group class offers more individualized attention to help participants further develop a mind and body connection while improving internal focus, balance, flexibility and strength at each student's pace. Achieve a calm mind using the therapeutic breath and meditation techniques that yoga provides. (km)

name: Yoga: Gentle Yoga

age_range.raw_age_text: 15 yrs +

description: Start with gentle movements and breathing practices to safely stretch the body and relax the nervous system. Postures are held for longer lengths of time and props are used to support a deep sense of letting go with maximum comfort. End with a guided meditation/relaxation that deeply calms the body, mind and spirit. This beginner-friendly program is geared toward individual needs and uses props. All students are welcome. (km)

name: Yoga: Hatha Yoga - Hybrid

age_range.raw_age_text: 15 yrs +

description: Benefit from an ancient system that attends to the total health of the body and mind. Yoga exercises are coordinated with deep breathing to help bring the body into proper alignment. Benefits include muscle balance, strength and elasticity, increased range of motion, improved coordination and improved function of internal glands and organs. Please bring an exercise mat and a large towel. Participants have the choice to take this class in-person or virtually via Zoom. (km)

name: Yoga: Intermediate/Advanced

age_range.raw_age_text: 16 yrs +

description: Find the peace amid the chaos with small group yoga. Experience the original and timeless mind and body practice. As you seek your internal focus, balance, flexibility and strength, calm the mind with breathing and meditation techniques that yoga has to offer. This class is for level intermediate/advanced. (km)

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 9 yrs

name: (ICE SKATING) Icette Prep Class

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 10 yrs but less than 18 yrs

description: This class is designated to expose skaters to specific elements and dance styles required for tryouts. Since Icette groups perform routines in the annual Northbrook-On-Ice show, the skills they learn and practice in this class will be incorporated into the routines they perform. description: In this timeless Neil Simon play, newly-minted teacher Leon is tasked with educating the people in a town cursed with chronic stupidity. In order to break the curse, Leon must educate the dumbest person in the village. Packed with puns and general buffoonery, this play will have actors and audience members alike laughing out-loud, non-stop! Come join us! This will be Northbrook Community Theatre's first all adult-cast play in their new Studio Theatre space. Auditions will be September 9 from 6:00-9:00pm, and will consist of reading scenes from the script. The rehearsal schedule is as follows: 9/13-- 10:00am-1:00pm 9/14, 9/16-- 6:30pm-9:00pm 9/22, 9/23-- 6:30pm-9:00pm 9/27-- 10:00am-1:00pm 9/28, 9/30-- 6:30pm-9:00pm 10/5-- 6:30pm-9:00pm 10/14-- 6:30pm-9:00pm 10/19-- 6:00pm-9:00pm 10/26-- 6:00pm-9:00pm 10/28-- 6:00pm-9:00pm 10/29-- 6:00pm-9:00pm Tech week rehearsals will be held to integrate sound, costumes, and lights. Tech rehearsals will be held 11/2, 11/3, 11/4, and 11/5 from 6:00-9:30pm. Performances will be November 6 and 7 at 7:00pm, and November 8 at 2:00pm.

name: Friday Night Pickleball Social Club

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: Join us for exciting and engaging evenings at the Friday Night Pickleball Club! Whether you're a seasoned player or just starting out, this program offers something for everyone. Half of the gym will be dedicated to open play pickleball, where you can enjoy friendly matches, meet new people, and have fun. Courts will be available for casual games, allowing you to play at your own pace and skill level. The other half of the gym will feature a pickleball pro who is available to answer your questions, help you work on techniques, and go over rules. This is a fantastic opportunity to improve your game, learn new strategies, and get personalized tips from an expert. Light refreshments will be provided throughout the evening, ensuring you stay energized and hydrated while you play and learn. Sign up for the season and enjoy the flexibility of attending at your leisure each Friday. Whether you come every week or just occasionally, the Friday Night Pickleball Club is designed to fit your schedule and provide a welcoming environment for all participants. No Class 9/11, 11/20, 11/27.

name: Get Golf Ready: Level 2 (Play with Confidence)

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 18 yrs but less than 80 yrs

description: Ready to take the next step on your journey into the game of golf? This class is geared for intermediate to advanced beginner golfers that have completed the level one class or have previous experience practicing at a driving range and playing a few times on a par 3 or 9 -hole course. In two, one and a half hour lessons and an on-course playing experience, our coaches will help you continue to build upon the fundamentals of your golf swing and golf game. For this level it is recommended that you practice and play outside of class. Classes will occur at the driving range at Heritage Oaks, and the last class will be an on-course playing lesson on the Legacy 9. Golf fitness will be further discussed in this class. Upon completion it is recommended that golfers continue onto the level three class, begin to practice and play on a regular basis, and join a beginner's golf league to further enhance their game.

name: Heritage Oaks Simulator League

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 18 yrs but less than 75 yrs

description: Compete in our indoor virtual golf league this offseason at Heritage Oaks. Full Swing Golf simulators feature the best graphics and real time ball flight on world class golf courses such as Pebble Beach, PGA National, St. Andrews Links, nine TPC Courses and more. League Format: Two-player teams will post a weekly combined gross score on six pre-determined golf courses during the regular season. All teams will play the same course conditions, with tee yardages designated for men and women. Teams will be awarded points during the regular season to earn a spot in the single elimination playoff bracket. (To qualify for the playoffs teams must complete at least 5 rounds by dates assigned) Weekly Closest to the Pin, Longest Drive and Longest Putt competitions add to the fun for all participants. A rolling handicap will be calculated during the regular season on a weekly basis using a triple bogey max, and will be applied during the playoff matches. During the playoffs each player will receive 70% of their handicap to determine the total net score. Ties will be broken using a scorecard playoff using the USGA method, last 6 holes, then last three holes, and finally the 9th hole. Regular Season: Oct. 19 - Nov 29 Playoffs: Nov 30 – Jan 10 Nine Hole Matches with a 9-Hole Championship Match League Fees: $60 per player for regular season and post season payouts, plus weekly contests (CTP, Long Drive, Long Putt) League rounds can be booked up to 14-days prior at the standard hourly simulator rental rates between 9am-8pm by calling the golf shop or on-line seven days in-advance. Enjoy the added flexibility to play any time that fits your schedule, and play rounds ahead of time as needed. Rules and Eligibility: Must be 21 years of age or older.

name: Northbrook Pickleball Co-Ed League - 60+ Intermediate

age_range.raw_age_text: 60 yrs +

description: Enjoy a fun, social and competitive league that allows you to play with a variety of players each week as you look to make your way to the top court. Register individually. Participants will play five games each week. Our leagues are categorized by skill level. We kindly request that you carefully review the description of each level and register for the one that best matches your abilities. Advanced Beginner (2.0): Players at this level understand the rules, know how to keep score, can hit forehands, backhands, and volleys, and can serve accurately. They also know where to stand when serving and returning. Low Intermediate (2.5): Players at this level know the basic rules and the two-bounce rule, can hit forehands and backhands with direction, serve accurately, sustain a dink rally, volley with some direction, understand the fundamentals, and keep score accurately. Intermediate (3.0): Players at this level can hit medium-paced forehands and backhands, serve with depth and accuracy, control a dink rally, hit medium-paced third-shot drops, and volley with direction. They understand the fundamentals of the game, positioning, and may have tournament experience. High Intermediate (3.5): Players at this level can use forehands and backhands with moderate control, consistently get serves and returns in, serve deep, and return deep. They can sustain medium-length dink rallies, control the height and depth of dink shots, and understand the variation of pace for dink shots. Advanced (4.0): Players at this level possess all the skills mentioned above and are accurate with overhead shots, can sustain dink rallies with control, height, and pace, consistently execute third-shot drops from the baseline, and can switch between soft and power shots. They can also block and return fast, hard volleys and are aware of their partner’s position on the court.

name: Northbrook Theatre Youth Company-Friday Cast

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 8 yrs but less than 15 yrs

description: Northbrook Theatre Youth Company is a recreational theatre program that creates quality productions with young actors. They perform age-appropriate musicals, suitable for family viewing. Young children will have the opportunity to grow through the performing arts as they work with professional staff and perform onstage - an exciting and rewarding experience. Gothic outsider teenager Lydia Deetz is adapting to life with a new step-mother and life in a new home, and is delighted to discover her new house is haunted by the kind and gentle, recently deceased couple named Barbara and Adam, as well as Beetlejuice, a zany demon with a real zest for life. Beetlejuice quickly turns the lives of Lydia, Barbara, and Adam upside down when he releases a world of chaos, comedy, and the unexpected! Auditions for Beetlejuice JR. will be held 8/25 and 8/26 from 4:00-8:00 pm. Callbacks (if necessary) will be held on 8/27 from 4:00-7:00pm. All participants should fill out the Google form at the bottom of their registration receipt to schedule an audition appointment. Auditions will be confirmed on a rolling basis beginning on Monday, 8/10. For auditions, actors should bring sheet music with 16-32 bars of a song to sing in-style of Beetlejuice. Actors should dress prepared to move, as they will be asked to complete a short dance portion at the audition. Actors will also be asked to read a scene from the script. Actors have the option to sign-up for the Beetlejuice JR audition workshop on 8/27 to help familiarize them with the audition proces! Friday cast rehearsals will be held on Fridays from 4:30pm-7:00pm, and Sundays from 11am-1pm from 8/31-10/11. Additional Friday cast rehearsals will be held on 9/14 from 4:30-7:00pm, 9/19, from 11:00am-1:00pm, 9/28 from 4:30-7pm, and 10/3 from 4-6pm. Tech week rehearsals will be held to integrate sound, costumes, and lights. The tech week schedule is as follows: 10/12 from 4:30-8:00pm, 10/18 from 4:30-8:00pm, and 10/18 from 10am-12:30pm. Performances will be held on 10/23 at 7pm and 10/25 at 1pm. No rehearsal 9/11 or 9/20.

name: Pickleball Co-Ed League - Advanced Beginner/Low Intermediate

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: Enjoy a fun, social and competitive league that allows you to play with a variety of players each week as you look to make your way to the top court. Register individually. Participants will play five games each week. Our leagues are categorized by skill level. We kindly request that you carefully review the description of each level and register for the one that best matches your abilities. Advanced Beginner (2.0): Players at this level understand the rules, know how to keep score, can hit forehands, backhands, and volleys, and can serve accurately. They also know where to stand when serving and returning. Low Intermediate (2.5): Players at this level know the basic rules and the two-bounce rule, can hit forehands and backhands with direction, serve accurately, sustain a dink rally, volley with some direction, understand the fundamentals, and keep score accurately. Intermediate (3.0): Players at this level can hit medium-paced forehands and backhands, serve with depth and accuracy, control a dink rally, hit medium-paced third-shot drops, and volley with direction. They understand the fundamentals of the game, positioning, and may have tournament experience. High Intermediate (3.5): Players at this level can use forehands and backhands with moderate control, consistently get serves and returns in, serve deep, and return deep. They can sustain medium-length dink rallies, control the height and depth of dink shots, and understand the variation of pace for dink shots. Advanced (4.0): Players at this level possess all the skills mentioned above and are accurate with overhead shots, can sustain dink rallies with control, height, and pace, consistently execute third-shot drops from the baseline, and can switch between soft and power shots. They can also block and return fast, hard volleys and are aware of their partner’s position on the court. No class 9/21

With roots in Chinese medicine, martial arts, and philosophy, qigong is accessible to people of all ages and fitness levels, offering a holistic approach to health and relaxation. Free for TPAC members

description: Taekwondo, one of the newest Olympic sports, is a 2,000-year-old martial art, offering a variety of benefits for people of all ages and physical abilities. Students have the opportunity to improve concentration, self-esteem, achieve lifelong physical fitness, and learn self-defense skills. Classes are taught under the direction of Grand Master Ki Hong Kim (9th Dan Kukkiwon World Taekwondo Headquarters). All students should talk to their instructor on the first day to get sized for a uniform which costs $50 cash or check. Uniforms are required to complete the class and to test for belt rank. Belt testing is offered through KH Kim Taekwondo, at an additional fee. Tests happen at the instructor's discretion when the student has learned the appropriate skills. All green belt students (Ages 7 yrs and up) are required to have complete sparring gear, which is purchased from the Instructor. Students will develop heightened focus, mental discipline, and strategic thinking, while enhancing their cardiovascular conditioning, flexibility, body control, and the beginning of mastery-level material to prepare students not only to earn their black belt, but to embody the role of a martial artist at the highest level. No Class 9/7 & 9/21.

description: Step into the spotlight and join us for a seniors-only production of The Music Man SR! This welcoming musical theatre experience is designed for adults ages 55 and up and combines performance opportunities with theatre education in a fun, supportive environment. Participants will learn the fundamentals of putting on a musical production, including acting, singing, stage movement, character development, rehearsal techniques, and performance skills. No previous theatre experience is required. Rehearsals are held Tuesday mornings, with additional Monday morning rehearsals beginning in November as performance day approaches. Whether you're a seasoned performer or stepping onto the stage for the first time, you'll enjoy building confidence, making new friends, and bringing this beloved classic to life. name: Adult Tennis Novice 2

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 18 yrs but less than 80 yrs

description: For players that have that have taken Novice I as well as those that have more consistency and experience. Emphasis is on introducing strategy to pair with stroke fundamentals.

name: Chair Yoga Saturday

age_range.raw_age_text: 50 yrs +

description: Increase flexibility, engage muscles, improve breathing and increase energy in Chair Yoga. Learn yoga techniques with a few modifications so you can move comfortably with the support of a chair. This class does not require participants to get on the floor. Class may involve optional exercises with light weights. No class 9/5, 9/19. (AV)

name: Tennis All Star Academy 7-10yr

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 7 yrs but less than 10y 11m 3w

description: Promotion from Quickstart or pro approval from evaluation required. This class is suitable for beginner players ages 8-10. Players continue to develop fundamentals using transition balls. Emphasis is on shot consistency, directional control, and speed control.

name: Tennis Green Dot Academy

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 7 yrs but less than 11 yrs

description: Promotion from All Star Academy or pro approval from evaluation required. This class is suitable for beginner players ages 10-11. Introduction to more live ball drills, point play, and more advanced rally skills. Playing strategy will be implemented on a full size court. (NA)

name: Adult Tennis Novice I

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: If you've never played tennis, or haven't played in awhile, this class is for you. Brush up on your strokes and strategy in a play oriented atmosphere. (NA)

name: Gentle Yoga & Meditation August

age_range.raw_age_text: 50 yrs +

description: With a blend of yoga mat work and guided meditation, you'll discover relaxation, flexibility and overall wellbeing. A great addition to your current yoga practice or a calming new part to your wellness routine. Relieve stress, connect with your body and leave feeling refreshed! No class 9/5. (AV)

name: Junior Tennis Academy 11-14yr

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 11 yrs but less than 14y 11m

description: Promotion from Green Ball Academy or pro approval from evaluation required. This class is suitable for qualified beginners. Students will be leveled within the class. Focus of instruction is on skill set improvement and application to competitive play.

name: Tennis Quickstart 1 (4-5yr)

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 4 yrs but less than 5y 11m 3w

description: Class focus is on basic fundamentals of hand eye coordination, balance, and agility. Fun games are designed to develop skills of movement, catching, throwing, ball tracking, and racquet handling.

name: Tennis Quickstart 2 (6-7yr)

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 7y 11m 3w

description: In addition to basic fundamentals, emphasis is on rally skills necessary for progression to the next level.

name: Tennis Quickstart II

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 7y 11m

description: In addition to basic fundamentals, emphasis is on rally skills necessary for progression to the next level. (NA)

name: Junior Beginner 11-14 Yrs

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 11 yrs but less than 14y 11m

description: This class is suitable for beginners including those that have had some tennis experience but have difficulty sustaining a slow rally and struggle with basic serve fundamentals.

name: High School Tennis Drill & Match Play

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 13 yrs but less than 18 yrs

description: This class is for high school varsity and tournament level players. (NA)

name: Tennis All Star Academy

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 7 yrs but less than 10 yrs

description: Promotion from Quickstart or pro approval from evaluation required. This class is also suitable for beginner players ages 8-10. Players continue to develop fundamentals using transition balls. Emphasis is on shot consistency, directional control, and speed control. (NA)

name: Tot Rock

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 1 yr but less than 2y 6m

description: Sing, dance, play, learn, and imagine with us! This movement-based program uses music to facilitate learning. Activities include use of rhythm instructions and movement props, work on gross and fine motor skills, including balance and coordination, and engagement of imaginative play. All classes are structured and include early listening and following directions skills. Get more information at www.rockitkids.com. (KT)

name: Kid Rock I

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 2 yrs but less than 3y 11m

description: Sing, dance, play, learn, and imagine with us! This movement-based program uses music to facilitate learning. Activities include use of rhythm instruments and movement props, work on gross and fine motor skills, including balance and coordination, and engagement of imaginative play. All classes are structured and include early listening and following directions skills. Get more information at www.rockitkids.com. (KT)

name: Family Rock

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 1 yr but less than 5y 11m

description: In Family Rock, we all rock together, with the youngest children learning from the older children! This movement-based program uses music to facilitate learning. Activities include use of rhythm instruments and movement props, work on gross and fine motor skills, including balance and coordination, and engagement of imaginative play. All classes are structured and include early listening and following directions. skills. Get more information at www.rockitkids.com. (KT)

name: Baby Rock

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 3m but less than 1y 3m

description: Wiggle and giggle with us! Baby Rock is a unique combination of sensory experiences with stimulating music and exercises to help strengthen and stretch your baby! Activities will include sing alongs, exposure to simple instruments and sensory props, motion exercises, bubbles, and more! Get ready for a rockin' good time with your tiniest dancer! www.rockitkids.com (CH)

name: Kid Rock II

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 3 yrs but less than 5y 11m

description: Maracas and clackers and tambourines, too; it's musical fun just for you! Our active, music-based, creative play programs include songs and rhymes, rhythm and coordination, fine and gross motor, imagination and sensory, listening and following directions skills, and more! Structured activities are age appropriate by class and include use of engaging rhythm instruments, movement props, and sensory materials. Sing, dance, play, learn and imagine! www.rockitkids.com (KT)

name: Indoor Cycling

age_range.raw_age_text: 14 yrs +

description: Join us for a fun and exciting workout that will effectively train every part of your body! Each 45-minute indoor cycling class will focus on cardio challenges and hill climbs that are suited for all participant levels. Each bike has a personalized computer that will track the number of calories you burned, how far you went, and your pace. Bring water and a towel to class. A heart rate monitor is optional, but highly recommended (DC). Free for ARC Fit and Plus Pass members—your discount will be applied at checkout. Non-members may register on the day of the class.

name: Parlez-vous francais?  I Speak French- Zoom (7-11 yrs.)

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 7 yrs but less than 12y 1m

description: Join us right from your living room as we explore new cultures and learn the French and Italian languages via the interactive Zoom platform! Each session covers new material. Taught live by a Language in Action, Inc. instructor. Zoom login information will be emailed to participants before the first class. (CH)

name: ARC a Diem

age_range.raw_age_text: 14 yrs +

description: Join us for a coach inspired group daily workout. Your certified group fitness coach will lead you through a unique and challenging full-body workout using rowers, indoor cycling bikes, and TRX straps. Each 45 minute workout will focus on strength, endurance, and cardiorespiratory fitness. Get ready to have fun, make friends, and get into your best shape! Free for ARC Fit and Plus Pass members—your discount will be applied at checkout. Non-members may register on the day of the class.

name: WERQ at Camelot

age_range.raw_age_text: 14 yrs +

description: WERQ® is the fiercely fun dance fitness workout class based on pop, rock, and hip hop music taught by Certified Fitness Professionals. The WERQ® warmup previews the dance steps used in class and the WERQ® cooldown includes balance and yoga-inspired poses. Are you ready to WERQ®? Free for ARC Fit and Plus Pass members—your discount will be applied at checkout. Non-members may register on the day of the class.

name: Restorative Yoga

age_range.raw_age_text: 14 yrs +

description: In restorative yoga, we learn learn how to allow ourselves to slow down, be supported, pay attention, grow present, and become comfortable with "being" rather than our usual "doing". This beginner friendly class will focus on stretching, breathing and holding postures that will soothe our overstimulated sympathetic nervous system, and find relief from the stress of our busy lives. Free for ARC Fit and Plus Pass members—your discount will be applied at checkout. Non-members may register on the day of the class.

name: 26|27 Vibe BROS Interest

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 6 yrs but less than 13 yrs

description: Interested in joining EPAA’s all-boys competition group? Participants will meet once a week on Tuesdays 4:15-4:45pm at Pioneer to learn and practice their dances. They will perform at local events and compete at two local competitions throughout the season. No audition required. The program will need a minimum of 5 dancers to run. Those that register to show interest will be contacted by September 1. Please email Kate at kschwarz@ahpd.org with questions.

name: Tuesday Deep Water Running at Pioneer

age_range.raw_age_text: 16 yrs +

description: Experience a low-impact, high-intensity workout suspended in the deep end of the pool. Using buoyancy belts (provided), you’ll stay afloat while running through water-based drills that build endurance, strength, and cardiovascular fitness—all without joint strain. (DC) Free for ARC Splash and Plus Pass members—your discount will be applied at checkout. Non-members may register on the day of the class.

name: Strength & Sculpt

age_range.raw_age_text: 14 yrs +

description: A total-body workout designed to build strength, define muscles, and boost endurance. This class combines targeted strength training with functional movements and finishing stretches to leave you feeling strong, energized, and sculpted from head to toe. (DC) Free for ARC Fit and Plus Pass members—your discount will be applied at checkout. Non-members may register on the day of the class.

name: Pilates

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 18 yrs but less than 99 yrs

description: Designed for all fitness levels, this Mat-based Pilates class focuses on core strength, stability, posture, flexibility, and proper breath control. Through guided instruction, you'll learn fundamental Pilates exercises using slow, controlled movements with an emphasis on challenging the core muscles. (DC)

name: Indoor Cycling

age_range.raw_age_text: 14 yrs +

description: Join us for a fun and exciting workout that will effectively train every part of your body! Each 45-minute indoor cycling class will focus on cardio challenges and hill climbs that are suited for all participant levels. A heart rate monitor is optional, but highly recommended (DC). Free for ARC Fit and Plus Pass members—your discount will be applied at checkout. Non-members may register on the day of the class.

name: Bridge Beginning

age_range.raw_age_text: 50 yrs +

description: Never learned to play Bridge in college? It’s not too late to join the fun! Learn the Standard American Bridge form, language, the mechanics of bidding and playing structured hands. No prior Bridge experience necessary! (AV)

name: Gentle Yoga

age_range.raw_age_text: 14 yrs +

description: Gentle Yoga is a slow, calming style of yoga that focuses on simple movements, light stretching, and deep breathing. It’s designed to improve flexibility, reduce stress, and promote relaxation without intense physical strain. Gentle yoga is suitable for beginners, older adults, or anyone looking for a low-impact, practice that supports both body and mind. Free for ARC Fit and Plus Pass members—your discount will be applied at checkout. Non-members may register on the day of the class.

name: Meet the Parrots

age_range.raw_age_text: 50 yrs +

description: Enter a bird paradise right in Arlington Heights! Parrot Stars is a one of a kind local pet shop focused on parrot education, conservation and sharing a love for birds. During the hour-long visit, browse the shop, meet their resident parrots up close and perch a bird on your hand! After, walk or drive to a self-pay brunch at Egg House in Arlington Heights. Attendees get a 10% senior discount! Meet at Parrot Stars, located at 115 N. Arlington Heights Rd, Arlington Heights. Transportation not provided. (AV)

name: Barre Class at Pioneer

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: The Barre workout is a high energy, full-body workout set to upbeat music. The class moves swiftly from cardio, to ballet barre, to core work on a mat. Ballet-inspired techniques (although no ballet experience necessary!) are used to develop lean muscle mass while improving balance, flexibility, and range of motion. It is an exciting body and mind workout that bridges the worlds of dance and Pilates. Please bring your own Yoga Mat to Class. Instructor: Stephanie (DC) Free for ARC Fit and Plus Pass members—your discount will be applied at checkout. Non-members may register on the day of the class.

name: NEW! Lunch and Play

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 3 yrs but less than 6 yrs

description: Children are introduced to a variety of sports including basketball, floor hockey, football, kickball, soccer, t-ball and other sports and group games. The goal is to provide the opportunity for each child to develop motor skills and nurture his/her growth socially through teamwork and good sportsmanship. Children eat lunch with the coaches, then play sports in the gym. (JD)

name: Tuesday Shallow Water at Pioneer

age_range.raw_age_text: 16 yrs +

description: Enjoy a refreshing, full-body workout in the shallow end of the pool. This class combines cardio, strength, and flexibility exercises using the natural resistance of water to tone muscles and improve endurance—while keeping it easy on the joints (DC). Free for ARC Splash and Plus Pass members—your discount will be applied at checkout. Non-members may register on the day of the class.

Instructors guide you through correct technique as you work with resistance tubes and weight plates, as well as body weight exercises like crunches and hovers. name: Innovation & Indulgence: A Day In Racine Tour

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: INNOVATION & INDULGENCE: A DAY IN RACINE SC JOHNSON CAMPUS TOUR LUNCH AT REEFPOINT BREW HOUSE SHOPPING AT O&H BAKERY Racine, Wisconsin Monday, September 14, 2026 8:15 AM - 4:15 PM Explore the home of SC Johnson in Racine, Wisconsin, where household brands like Pledge, Glade, Off and Windex are produced. This docent-guided walking tour combines iconic Frank Lloyd Wright architecture with a modern, eco-friendly workplace. Appreciate stunning architecture while learning about the company's history and its impact. Bring a state ID or driver’s license for tour check-in. The tour includes indoor and outdoor spaces. Guests should be comfortable standing, walking and climbing stairs. Elevators are available in Fortaleza Hall and Waxbird Commons. The Golden Rondelle Theater, Fortaleza Hall and Waxbird Commons are walker-accessible and the main floor of the Great Workroom is accessible via ramp. The Research Tower is accessible only via stairs. After the tour, enjoy lunch at Reefpoint Brew House, overlooking Racine Harbor. Lunch includes a non-alcoholic beverage and a cash bar is available. Entree choices are: Reuben (marbled rye, corned beef, Swiss cheese,1000 Island and sauerkraut) with fries Italian Bella (tomato focaccia bun, caramelized onions, grilled portobello mushroom, roasted red peppers, spinach tomatoes and pesto aioli) with fries Brew House Burger (brioche bun, lettuce, tomatoes and red onions) with fries Fisherman’s Catch (pretzel bun, fried cod, lettuce, tomatoes, red onions, pickles and tartar sauce) with fries Cobb Salad (mixed greens, bacon bits, smoked turkey, tomatoes, avocado, egg, blue cheese crumbles and choice of dressing) Following lunch, stop at O&H Danish Bakery, renowned for its savory and sweet treats, including Kringles! Purchase something delicious for dessert or to take home for later. Orders can be placed in advance at www.ohdanishbakery.com to ensure they will have what you want. When ordering and checking out, choose their Racine West location on Washington Avenue.

description: Program Details: Ages: 5–12 years Class Length: 40 minutes Program Overview: Swim School provides a structured, skill-based progression for swimmers of all experience levels, with the goal of developing confident, capable swimmers and preparing them for future swim team participation. name: Cantigny Gardens Tour

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: CANTIGNY GARDENS Wheaton, Illinois Monday, September 21, 2026 9:00 AM – 4:00 PM Cantigny is a 500-acre public park and estate that was the former home of Colonel Robert R. McCormick, a long-time editor and publisher of the Chicago Tribune. Our day begins in the Visitor Center viewing a short film with background information on Cantigny’s history, followed by a docent-led tour of the gardens. After lunch, enjoy time exploring The First Division Museum, Tank Park and McCormick House. Each lunch includes a cookie, chips and a choice of a non-alcoholic beverage: The Italian: Salami, Capicola, Provolone, Giardiniera, shredded lettuce and red wine vinaigrette on an herbed focaccia bun Chicken Salad Sandwich: Whole roasted chicken, grapes, celery and aioli on a fresh croissant Roast Beef: Thinly sliced roast beef, lettuce, tomato, Provolone and mayo on a fresh hoagie roll Smoked Chicken and Cranberry: Smoked chicken breast, cranberry chutney, Swiss cheese, baby greens and Dijon-mayo on an herbed focaccia bun Greens and Grains Salad: Mixed greens, herbed quinoa and farro, cherry tomatoes, feta cheese, avocado, red onion, shaved radish and honey white balsamic dressing Cantigny Cobb: Chopped romaine, hard-boiled egg, tomatoes, bacon, scallions, crumbled goat cheese, chopped chicken and green goddess dressing

name: Experience Pullman Tour

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: EXPERIENCE PULLMAN! PULLMAN EXHIBIT HALL, BUS TOUR & VISITOR CENTER OF PULLMAN NATIONAL HISTORICAL PARK Chicago, Illinois Friday, September 25, 2026 8:30 AM - 3:30 PM Must register by September 9. Pullman is a remarkable place where American history, innovation, and community come to life. Begin at the Pullman Exhibit Hall with a short video exploring Pullman's history and its role in American industry and labor. Browse historic photographs and artifacts that bring the community's story to life. Then take a guided bus tour through the Pullman Historic District, focused on the beautifully preserved exteriors of homes and public buildings from the 1880s. Along the way, learn about the neighborhood's distinctive architecture and lasting community significance. After enjoying a boxed lunch at the Exhibit Hall, a short bus ride brings us to Pullman National Historical Park to explore the visitor center exhibits and historic grounds at your own pace. The boxed lunches include a choice of sandwich, with garden pasta salad, fresh fruit salad and a salted caramel bar for dessert. A bottle of water is also included. Please choose a first and second sandwich option, as the caterer requires specific sandwich counts. Effort will be made to provide everyone with their first choice. The sandwich choices are: Roast Beef & Cheddar Smoked Ham & Swiss Roast Turkey & Colby Jack Albacore Tuna

Kids will experience a hurricane dramatization to be sure their bridge is structurally sound! Participants may take their edible creation home or eat it on the spot! Kids will have such a creepy blast; they won’t even realize they are building self-esteem, boosting their socialization, and acquiring new S.T.E.M. concepts! name: Fork & Cork: House of Gerhard Tour

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: HOUSE OF GERHARD SHOPPING AT MARS CHEESE CASTLE Kenosha, Wisconsin Tuesday, October 6, 2026 10:45 AM – 4:15 PM Prost! October is the perfect time to enjoy German food! Join us at the House of Gerhard for authentic German cuisine in an enchanting atmosphere filled with old-world charm. Lunch includes a choice of entrée, Chicken Spaetzle soup, homemade German hard rolls, sweet muffins and their signature dessert, the Strawberry Schaum Torte. Entrée options are: Bavarian Pot Roast: Tender sliced beef topped with brown gravy, served with red cabbage and mashed potatoes Roast Loin of Pork: Juicy center-cut pork with sage dressing and pork gravy, served with vegetables and mashed potatoes Roasted Chicken Breast: Boneless chicken breast with herb stuffing, served with vegetables and mashed potatoes Coffee, tea, and milk are included. A cash bar is available. After lunch, visit Mars Cheese Castle, a Wisconsin institution. Mars Cheese Castle features a specialty market offering more than 700 cheeses, wines and specialty items; an in-house bakery with desserts, kringles and freshly baked bread; as well as a pub known for its Wisconsin beers and famous Bloody Marys.

description: The Arlington Muskies Swim Team is a competitive swim team for ages 6-18 that puts an emphasis on improving strokes, building endurance, being a part of the team and helping swimmers grow a lifelong passion for the sport. The Arlington Muskies are members of the Northern Illinois Swim Conference. Muskies travel to neighboring park districts to compete in meets, swimmers will have the opportunity to compete in over 8 dual swim meets. The Winter season will begin on Tuesday, October 6th and go until Saturday, February 27th. Each registrant will get access to the Muskie website where they will receive communications and access to , meet registration and results, as well as access to the team spirit wear shop. Muskies are 4-time defending NISC “A” Division Champions!

name: Jr.Coaching - Muskies

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 14y 6m but less than 18 yrs

Our coaches will be able to swim and participate in practice and compete at meets. Our introductory coaches will be asked to help out during 10 and under practices to help our young swimmers develop. We just ask that our junior coaches help out for at least 8 hours per month. The prerequisites are to have competed in either the winter season and/or the summer season on Muskies. Please reach out to Ila Nathanson at inathanson@ahpd.org if you have any questions.

name: Chicago Sports Legends & Landmark Tour

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: CHICAGO SPORTS LEGENDS & LANDMARK! SOLDIER FIELD TOUR & CHICAGO SPORTS MUSEUM LUNCH AT HARRY CARAY’S 7TH INNING STRETCH Monday, October 12, 2026 8:45 AM - 4:30 PM Go behind-the-scenes at Soldier Field! Since its founding in 1924, Soldier Field has served as a symbol of tradition and excellence, honoring the men and women of the armed services. Today, it is the home of the Chicago Bears (NFL) and the Chicago Fire FC (MLS). Whether you're a die-hard sports fan or a history enthusiast, this tour offers you unprecedented access to the heart of the action! Then take a lunch break at Harry Caray’s 7th Inning Stretch. Lunch includes a choice of entree, a mixed baby greens salad, a funfetti cupcake and a non-alcoholic beverage station. Entree choices are: Short Rib Italian Beef Sandwich with Provolone, giardiniera, au jus, Parmesan & Romano cheese, garlic bread and french fries Chinese Chicken Salad with Chinese long beans, toasted cashews, napa cabbage, sesame seeds, carrots, wontons, mandarin oranges and sesame soy dressing Turkey Burger with roasted roma tomato, baby spinach, smoked mozzarella, basil pesto, red wine vinaigrette, brioche bun and french fries A cash bar is available. After lunch, visit The Chicago Sports Museum. This museum combines high-tech interactive experiences with unique sports memorabilia and an impressive collection of game-used treasures and artifacts. The 23,000-square-foot space celebrates all of Chicago's major sports teams.

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: MENOPAUSE THE MUSICAL PARAMOUNT THEATRE LUNCH AT THE FIRESIDE GRILL Aurora & Sugar Grove, Illinois Saturday, October 17, 2026 11:30 AM – 6:00 PM Menopause The Musical is a hilarious and lighthearted tribute to "The Change." Set in a department store lingerie sale, the show follows four diverse women who bond over shared experiences of menopausal symptoms such as hot flashes, memory loss and night sweats while singing and dancing to parodies of classic pop songs from the 1960s, 70s and 80s. Before the performance, enjoy lunch at the Fireside Grille. Each entrée is served with a garden salad, bread and butter, vegetables, smashed potatoes and an ice cream sundae. name: Jailhouse Rock In Joliet Tour

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: JAILHOUSE ROCK IN JOLIET! OLD JOLIET PRISON & ILLINOIS ROCK & ROLL MUSEUM SELF-PAY LUNCH AT PROTILLO'S IN SHOREWOOD Joliet & Shorewood, Illinois Wednesday, October 21, 2026 8:45 AM - 5:00 PM This 90-minute walking tour of the Old Joliet Prison is led by knowledgeable docents and tour guides from the Joliet Area Historical Museum. The tour provides an overview of the prison's history, from its opening in 1858 to its closure in 2002. Explore various historic buildings throughout the 16-acre prison site and hear fascinating accounts of prison life, notable inmates, escapes and the evolution of the facility. The Joliet Prison tour is entirely outdoors, rain or shine. The tour covers a considerable distance with some areas not fully paved or in poor condition. Please dress appropriately for the weather and wear comfortable walking or hiking shoes.. After touring the prison, we will stop for a quick self-pay lunch at Portillo’s in Shorewood. Bring money for lunch. Following lunch, tour The Illinois Rock & Roll Museum, which celebrates the rich musical legacy of Illinois and its significant impact on rock and roll history. The museum honors legendary artists, producers and industry influencers. As a cultural hub on the iconic Route 66, the museum connects generations through music, preserving the stories and sounds that have shaped America’s musical landscape.

description: Join the Park District's annual Trunk or Treat event on Saturday, 10/24, from 10a-12:30pm at Pioneer Park, 500 S. Fernandez Ave. This family-friendly event celebrates Halloween by providing a unique way for children ages 2-13 to trick-or-treat with parental supervision. Participating organizations have the opportunity to introduce and publicize their brand to participating families in a festive atmosphere while providing a fun service to the community. Registration is free and includes parking for one sedan to SUV sized vehicle. To ensure that your vehicle is event-ready and on-theme and that the treat line moves safely and smoothly: Come in costume and decorate your vehicle in a Halloween theme of your choice. Bring Halloween handouts (packaged candy or toy) for 1,000 children. You may also pass out a coupon for your business, but this must be in addition to your Halloween treat. We do not provide tables, chairs, or access to electricity, so be sure to bring any supplies you may need. All supplies, including decorations and signage, must fit in/ slightly in front of two standard parking spaces. Generators, music that projects beyond the immediate area of your vehicle, and games that slow the trick-or-treat line are not allowed. Access to the parking lot opens at 8:30am and closes at 9:30am. Late vehicles will not be allowed in the lot. If your organization would like to have a larger Trunk or Treat impact, contact Amy Lewandowski, Director of Marketing, at alewandowski@ahpd.org, to inquire about limited sponsorship opportunities for this event.

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 9 yrs but less than 99 yrs

name: Windy City Diving Level 1 - Session 2

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 8 yrs but less than 18 yrs

description: Level 1 The beginner diving class is an introduction to the sport of springboard diving and is designated to teach the safe and proper way to use the springboard. Any individual 8-18 years old who has an interest in diving, can swim comfortably in deep water, and dive in head first off the side of the pool deck into deep water can take this class. Students will be taught a forward approach and a back press. They will progress to forward and backward dives as well as other skills based on ability. Your child must be comfortable in deep water and be able to swim 20 yards unassisted in deep water to enroll in this class. Swimming instruction is not provided in diving lessons. All participants must become an AAU Diving Athlete member- $20. Register online at aausports.org/Join-AAU. Proof of AAU Diving registration MUST be shown on first day of class. All diving lessons are video recorded.

name: Adult Pickleball Beginner

The slower pace of this class will give players the opportunity to develop the skills needed to play this fun and energetic game. All equipment will be provided. (MH)

name: Swim School

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 5 yrs but less than 12y 11m

description: Program Details: Ages: 5–12 years Class Length: 40 minutes Program Overview: Swim School provides a structured, skill-based progression for swimmers of all experience levels, with the goal of developing confident, capable swimmers and preparing them for future swim team participation. Instructors focus on stroke technique, lateral breathing, diving, endurance, and essential water safety skills in a fun and supportive environment. With clearly defined levels and consistent feedback, swimmers advance at their own pace while building strong technique and confidence. Skills Taught: Swim School is taught in a motivating group environment that encourages peer learning and confidence. description: THE WAITING LIST FOR HIS ACTIVITY IS NOW FULL. All aboard our Storytime Train! We manage this wait list carefully and make every effort to include as many passengers as are allowed. name: Adult Ballet

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 18 yrs but less than 99 yrs

description: Beginning level classes focus on the basics of ballet including proper placement and posture; body positions, plies, tendus, battements, and port de bras. Emphasis will be placed on understanding technique, as well as instilling an appreciation and enjoyment of the movement. Advanced levels are a continual study of fundamentals, extended to emotional expression and precision, as well as developing fluid artistic control. Ballet is the basis of all other dance forms and can strongly enhance any athletic activity. We strongly encourage that ballet be taken in conjunction with any other dance class.

name: Adult Hip Hop

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 18 yrs but less than 99 yrs

description: Hip-Hop is a high intensity dance form that is often paired with the latest hip-hop music. Having evolved from “street dancing”, Hip-Hop has an edgy component which is taught through isolations of the body in addition to alternating between smooth and quick, sharp movements. This class will increase flexibility and coordination by challenging the pace at which the dancer’s body can move. This class helps express personality through movement that allows for a little attitude.

name: Bachata Latin Dance Class

age_range.raw_age_text: 9 yrs +

description: Bachata is a dance that is based on an easy-to-follow sequence of three on-beat steps, with a tap marking the fourth beat. It is styled with a fluid sway of the hips which is mesmerizing to watch and just wonderful to dance! Bachata’s simplicity makes it a beginner-friendly dance, while the opportunity for musical interpretation it provides makes it truly addictive for dancers of all levels. Class is open to individuals and couples. We recommend that you avoid wearing gym shoes to sessions so you can turn smoothly on the floor.

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 13 yrs but less than 18 yrs

Emphasis will be placed on understanding technique, as well as instilling an appreciation and enjoyment of the movement. Advanced levels are a continual study of fundamentals, extended to emotional expression and precision, as well as developing fluid artistic control. Ballet is the basis of all other dance forms and can strongly enhance any athletic activity. We strongly encourage that ballet be taken in conjunction with any other dance class.

name: Hip Hop Advanced

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 13 yrs but less than 18 yrs

description: Hip-Hop is a high intensity dance form that is often paired with the latest hip-hop music. Having evolved from “street dancing”, Hip-Hop has an edgy component which is taught through isolations of the body in addition to alternating between smooth and quick, sharp movements. This class will increase flexibility and coordination by challenging the pace at which the dancer’s body can move. This class helps express personality through movement that allows for a little attitude.

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 7 yrs but less than 11 yrs

This challenges the student to connect on a deeper level to the dance and to become a part of the music.

name: Know and Grow Series: From Headstones to Hot Sausages - Expl

age_range.raw_age_text: 18 yrs +

description: Discover two distinctly Chicago experiences in one engaging Chicago outing. We will depart from Heritage Farm and journey to historic Rosehill Cemetery for a guided walking tour, where storytelling explores the city’s past through rich symbolism, and the notable figures who helped shape Chicago’s history. After our walking tour, we will head to Gene’s Sausage Shop and Delicatessen for a relaxed lunch of traditional sausages and/or pierogi. This program offers a thoughtful blend of culture, history, and German / Polish cuisine—ideal for all who enjoy experiencing the city through its stories and its food. Comfortable walking shoes are highly recommended.

This class is wonderful for anyone interested in joining their High School Dance Team.

name: Schaumburg Children's Theatre Audition: Mary Poppins Jr.

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 8 yrs but less than 18 yrs

description: Join us at auditions for our Fall Children's Theater show: the timeless classic, Mary Poppins Jr! Synopsis: Young Jane and Michael have sent many a nanny packing before Mary Poppins arrives on their doorstep. Using a combination of magic and common sense, she must teach the family members how to value each other again. Mary Poppins takes the children on many magical and memorable adventures, but Jane and Michael aren't the only ones upon whom she has a profound effect. Even grown-ups can learn a lesson or two from the nanny who advises that "Anything can happen if you let it." Advance preparation is NOT required for this audition! Please arrive between 5:00-8:00 p.m. You will be emailed an audition form to fill out. Please fill it out before audition day. Participants will audition in groups on a first-come first-called basis and will be dismissed after their group has finished. Callbacks will be Thursday, September 10th by invitation. This audition is open to ages 8-17. There is a casting fee of $220.00 per participant if cast in the show. Rehearsals will be Mon./Tues./Wed. from 5pm-8pm Mandatory tech rehearsals and performances are listed below: Tech: November 28th-December 3rd Performances: Fri. 12/4 at 7:00pm, Sat. 12/5 at 1:30pm and 7:00pm, and Sun. 12/6 at 1:30pm *Participants must be able to attend all tech rehearsals and performances *

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 12 yrs but less than 18 yrs

description: Hip-Hop is a high intensity dance form that is often paired with the latest hip-hop music. Having evolved from “street dancing”, Hip-Hop has an edgy component which is taught through isolations of the body in addition to alternating between smooth and quick, sharp movements. This class will increase flexibility and coordination by challenging the pace at which the dancer’s body can move. This class helps express personality through movement that allows for a little attitude.

description: The Elmhurst Park District invites you to honor a loved one or commemorate a special occasion with a permanent engraved brick paver. Pavers are ordered four times per year. The following are the cut-off dates for orders and the approximate date of installation: Order in By Installed By July 1st October 1st October 1st January 1st (weather permitting) January 1st April 1st (weather permitting) April 1st July 1st The dates above allow enough time for shipping and installation of pavers at the walk. Winter orders are installed as soon as the ground thaws. On occasion, the engraving company will be extremely busy and additional time will have to be allowed for engraving and delivery. Every effort will be made to install the pavers by the dates listed above. After the pavers are installed, a confirmation letter will be sent to the donor as official notification of installation.

The day concludes at the iconic Starbucks Reserve Roastery, where participants can experience small-batch coffee roasting, specialty beverages, and the immersive design of one of Starbucks’ flagship locations. The Park District will rototill and stake each area, you plant, cultivate and reap the harvest. Six water taps are available and are open 9 am - 9 pm, seven days a week. Weather permitting, growing season runs from May - November 1. A maximum of one garden plot per family is allowed. RETURNING PARTICIPANTS: We will continue to give returning customers (those who had plots in 2025) the option of keeping the same plot or entering the lottery for a new plot. Returning participants must register between February 21-March 13 to secure a plot for 2026. NEW PARTICIPANTS: Those who did not have a plot in 2025 WILL BE ABLE TO REGISTER BETWEEN MARCH 19 (Beginning at 8 am) AND APRIL 5 for any available plots. Available plots will be sold on a first come first served basis. A lottery will be held for plot selection. New gardeners that get a plot will receive more information on how the lottery to choose your plot works after April 5. The lottery for plot selection will be held on Wednesday, April 15 at 6:30 pm at the Kies Recreation Center. (AS)

description: Relax and de-stress as you are bathed by candlelight and sound at the historic Wilder Mansion. Experience the mental and physical health benefits of live sound meditation as you are guided on a journey in sound and deep listening by Certified Sound Bath and Meditation facilitator Dana Kraszczynski. A Sound Bath, or Sound Meditation, is a deep immersion in sound that is felt in your whole being. Find a comfortable seat or lie down and allow the soothing vibrations of singing bowls, flutes, and chimes to wash over your whole body, creating a gentle yet deeply transformative effect on your body and mind. The intention of this practice is to guide you into a state of deep relaxation. No special skills, abilities, or beliefs are required to receive the benefits. Please bring something comfortable to sit or lay down on such as a yoga mat, blankets, and/or pillows.

Leave the mental overload of the week behind and start your weekend off rested, calm, and emotionally balanced. (AS)

Luckily, the narrators are here to show you how to make it through New Years in one piece. This production is a crowd-pleasing whirlwind tour through the hilarious pitfalls that we all power through to make merry. Auditions: Oct 20. Watch as products move through the facility—from receiving and sorting to packing and shipping—using advanced robotics and innovative systems. This fascinating tour offers a unique glimpse into the fast-paced world of logistics and the process that gets millions of packages delivered to doorsteps every day. Lunch on your own after the tour. Buckle up for a short thrilling finale on Lake Michigan to top off your experience and cruise along the skyline at top Seadog speed! description: The simplified 24-step Tai Chi form is practiced for its many health benefits, including improvements in balance, flexibility and range of motion. Consistent practice helps to increase muscle strength and has been shown to benefit those with arthritis and osteoporosis. The gentle, low-impact movements are done slowly with little of no force or tension. The class is suitable for almost anyone and can be adapted to take into consideration most physical limitations.

age_range.raw_age_text: 50 yrs +

description: Take charge of your health with confidence! Join a nurse advocate for an informative and empowering session designed to help older adults better understand and navigate today’s healthcare system. Learn practical strategies for managing medications, preparing for doctor visits, understanding insurance options, and advocating for yourself or a loved one. The program will also highlight the benefits of choosing a trusted third party as a medical power of attorney to ensure your wishes are clearly communicated and honored. Learn helpful tools and resources to support independence, improve health outcomes, and help you feel confident making decisions about your care. Sponsored by Nurse Patient Allies.

name: Charleston, SC Diamond Tours

age_range.raw_age_text: 30 yrs +

description: Day 1: Depart your group's location in a spacious, video and restroom equipped motorcoach as you head for your destination: Charleston, South Carolina! This evening you will stay at an en route hotel. Day 2: Enjoy a Continental Breakfast. Today you will continue your journey, then enjoy a leisurely Dinner and check into a Charleston area hotel for a four night stay. Day 3: After a Continental Breakfast, you'll head to historic MIDDLETON PLACE. This impressive attraction contains 65 acres of America's oldest landscaping. After each member receives their welcome map, you'll experience the garden, animal stables, the Chapel, Rice Mill, and more! After lunch on your own and free time in Downtown Charleston, you'll enjoy a scenic HARBOR CRUISE. Enjoy the beauty of the Charleston Harbor and learn the rich history of the "Holy City". During this scenic and relaxing tour, you will see dozens of landmarks and points of interest as hundreds of years of history is covered. This evening, enjoy Dinner before heading back to your hotel for a good night's rest. Day 4: After a Continental Breakfast, you'll enjoy a GUIDED TOUR of McLeod Plantation Historic Site. Established in 1851, this important 37-acre Gullah/Geechee heritage site has been carefully preserved in recognition of its cultural and historical significance. Later, you'll enjoy lunch on your own in the “cultural heart of Charleston.” Next, you'll have some free time to explore The Historic Charleston City Market. Located downtown, this architecturally significant National Historic Landmark is home to eclectic shops, you won't find anywhere else. This continuous series of market buildings stretches four city blocks. Next you'll appreciate a short photo stop at the famed Angel Oak Tree, estimated to be 400 years old! This evening, enjoy Dinner before heading back to your hotel for a good night's rest. Day 5: After a Continental Breakfast, you'll enjoy both a GUIDED TOUR OF CHARLESTON and an intimate TOUR inside the HISTORIC CHARLESTON HOME: The Joseph Manigault House. The Manigault's descent from French Huguenots who fled religious persecution in Europe in the late 1600s. Afterwards, you'll visit the CHARLESTON TEA GARDEN. At this unique tea garden, your group will take a factory tour and see how tea is made, including tasting samples at the Tea Bar. A highlight of your tour includes a TROLLEY TOUR of the garden. This evening, enjoy Dinner before heading back to your hotel for a good night's rest. Day 6: Enjoy a Continental Breakfast at your hotel before leaving for a visit to the South Carolina State Museum in Columbia, SC. Tonight, you'll relax in an en route hotel. Day 7: Enjoy a Continental Breakfast before departing for home... a perfect time to chat with your friends about all the fun things you've done, the great sights you've seen and where your next group trip will take you! (Sun - Sat) Oct 25 - 31 2026 $1079* WOOD DALE PARK DISTRICT PRESENTS Charleston Motorcoach transportation 6 nights lodging including 4 consecutive nights in the Charleston area 10 meals: 6 breakfasts and 4 dinners Visit to The Historic Charleston City Market Relaxing Harbor Cruise in Charleston Visit to Famous and Historic Middleton Place Guided Tour of Charleston Tour of Historic Charleston Home 'The Joseph Manigault House' Admission to McLeod Plantation Historic Site Photo stop at Famous Angel Oak Tree & Visit to Charleston Tea Garden, Including a Trolley Ride For more pictures, video, and information visit: www.GroupTrips.com/wooddaleparkdistrict Departure: Wood Dale Park District, 111 E Foster Ave, Wood Dale, IL @ 8 am Jen Bolich - Wood Dale

name: Connections Dance Company

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 7 yrs but less than 18y 6m

description: The Connection Dance Company brings dancers from all our participating communities together to learn and grow as a team. It provides dedicated dancers the opportunity to study a variety of dance styles in more depth. This performing group is a year- round commitment. Our focus will be creating, leading, and guiding dancers on a disciplined and rewarding path that will instill the fundamentals of dance and performance. Company members are required to take 1 foundational technique class the entire season (Sept 2026-June 2027) in addition to company rehearsal. The Company will meet monthly on Fridays and will rotate rehearsal space between West Chicago, Winfield, Medinah and Wood Dale. They will also participate in 3-5 competitions community events throughout the year. Rehearsal and Performance Schedules will be available at the first class. Some additional rehearsals and performances will be during times outside of regularly scheduled rehearsal time. All experience levels are welcome. Please wear leotard, tights or comfortable form fitted clothing. Dancers will also need skin toned jazz shoes. The registration fee does not include Company Costume, Competition and Event fees which range from $200-300 for the year and due in October. It does include 40 hours of rehearsal time to rehearse choreography for 2 group routines. Please contact Lora@innovationartsconnection for details on the Connection Dance Company.

name: Do Art Productions: Acting/Improv Class

age_range.raw_age_text: Age at least 7 yrs but less than 14 yrs

location: Clauss Recreation Center- 555 W. Bryn Mawr Ave, Roselle IL, 60172
description: In this engaging and confidence-building acting program, participants explore a new emotion and visual acting skill. Through fun improv games and creative prompts (including pulling ideas from a “mystery hat”), kids learn how to express feelings, think on their feet, and work together in imaginative scenes. Throughout the program, students practice using voice tone and facial expressions, communicating through body language and movement, building confidence speaking in front of others, listening, reacting, and collaborating with peers. By the end of the program, participants leave with a strong toolkit of acting and communication skills they can use onstage, in school presentations, and in everyday social situations—all while having a blast in a supportive, playful environment. Registration deadline is September 18.

Each day includes enriching activi- ties designed to encourage creativity, learning, teamwork, and recreation. Participants may enjoy arts and crafts, games, STEM projects, sports, and special themed activities led by caring staff. name: Chiaravalle School-Cross Country

schedule.raw_schedule_text: Start date: Wednesday, September 23 2026. Schedule: Wednesdays, 5:00 PM - 6:00 PM , From September 23, 2026 until October 21, 2026 , Twiggs Park , Location: Twiggs Park | 1901 Simpson Street, Evanston, IL, 60201 Description: REGISTRATION DEADLINE: AUGUST 20 Our co-ed cross country program for 4th and 5th graders introduces young runners to the fun and fundamentals of distance running. Through engaging practices and friendly meets, students will build endurance, improve running form, and develop teamwork and perseverance. Biweekly meets will take place, with race distances ranging from 1 to 1.5 miles. Each participant will receive a team shirt to wear on race days. Volunteer coaches from each participating school will coordinate team practices. description: The fall Ultimate Disc league is open to youth ages 9-14. Ultimate frisbee is a fun, fast growing, non-contact sport that emphasizes teamwork and player leadership through self officiating. It is also an excellent crossover sport for athletes who play soccer, basketball, football, or lacrosse by helping develop conditioning, agility, cutting, field awareness, and hand eye coordination. Each league night, mixed gender teams will participate in a short practic focused on skill development through activities like throwing accuracy games, partner catching, Randy Moss drills, footwork games, and pulling contests, followed by league play. Great for multi-sport athletes looking to stay active and competitive during the fall season.
